findings.title: Replacing the destination drops its existing mode/ownership
findings.evidence: os.replace(tmp_path, path) swaps in the mkstemp file, which is created 0600 (umask-independent), so a pre-existing 0640/0644 state file becomes 0600 and owned by the writing euid; any reader running as another user or group loses access.
findings.recommendation: If the destination exists, stat it and os.chmod (and if privileged, os.chown) the temp file to the previous mode/owner before the rename; otherwise document explicitly that the file is always created 0600 and that callers must set permissions themselves.

findings.title: Symlinked state path is replaced instead of followed
findings.evidence: directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)) uses abspath, which does not resolve symlinks, so a path that is a symlink to another file is replaced by a regular file (the link is destroyed and the real target is never updated).
findings.evidence_quote: directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)) uses abspath, which does not resolve symlinks, so a path that is a symlink to another file is replaced by a regular file (the link is destroyed and the real target is never updated).
findings.recommendation: Resolve the destination with os.path.realpath (or refuse symlinked paths with an explicit error) before deriving the temp directory and calling os.replace, so the documented atomic-rename contract applies to the real file.

findings.title: Directory fsync failure reports failure after the write is already committed
findings.evidence: _fsync_directory(directory) runs after os.replace has already made the new state visible, so if the directory fsync raises (some filesystems return EINVAL/ENOTSUP, or EACCES on restrictive dirs) save_state raises even though the data is durably replaced, and the caller may believe the save failed and retry with stale data.

findings.recommendation: Wrap the directory fsync so known-unsupported errors (EINVAL, ENOTSUP, EBADF) are ignored and the function only signals success once os.replace has completed; re-raise other OSErrors only if you intend to report the save as failed.

findings.title: Atomic state writer ships with no tests
findings.evidence: def save_state(path, state) introduces file-persistence behaviour (temp-file creation, exception cleanup, os.replace, directory fsync, load_state corrupt-root error) with no accompanying test covering success, serialisation failure cleanup, or the non-dict-root ValueError.
findings.evidence_quote: def save_state(path, state) introduces file-persistence behaviour (temp-file creation, exception cleanup, os.replace, directory fsync, load_state corrupt-root error) with no accompanying test covering success, serialisation failure cleanup, or the non-dict-root ValueError.
findings.recommendation: Add tests asserting: successful round-trip via load_state; temp file is removed when json.dump raises on a non-serialisable value; load_state returns {} for a missing file and raises ValueError for a non-object root; and no .state-*.tmp files remain in the directory after a failed save.

findings.title: File descriptor leaks if wrapping the raw fd fails
findings.evidence: fd, tmp_path = tempfile.mkstemp( acquires a raw fd that is only owned by the context manager once os.fdopen succeeds; if that call itself raises, the cleanup path unlinks the temp file but never closes fd.

findings.recommendation: Wrap the fd in try/except immediately after mkstemp and close it with os.close(fd) when os.fdopen fails, or restructure so the fd is closed in a finally block when no handle was created.
